conventions.convention: Complex states use the standard Euclidean norm; componentwise realification into R^(2d) preserves that norm and interprets real-time differentiation and integration.
ETD2 uses the exponential-Euler predictor and coefficients phi_1−phi_2 and phi_2; inputs and displayed stages must belong to U.
Phi functions are evaluated by convergent series or integral representations, including at singular and zero matrices; matrix division is unnecessary.

Certification requires sound action, field, arithmetic, membership, and scalar-enclosure data. Backend calls have finite budgets and pre-call count bounds; work counters record actual declared work rather than wall-clock complexity.

Global estimates use T>0, N≥1, h=T/N, exact initial data, uniform regularity and Lipschitz bounds, and a common compact admissible tube. Constants may depend on the fixed finite matrix and dimension; no stiffness-uniform or unbounded-operator conclusion is asserted.
Real-time propagation uses A=−iH and is unitary; imaginary-time propagation uses −H and exhibits decay.

load_bearing.statement: For d≥1, A∈M_d(C), g:[0,T]×U→C^d and t≥0, h>0 with t+h≤T, inputs and displayed stages lie in U. Exponential Euler is e^(hA)y+h phi_1(hA)g(t,y). ETD2 uses that predictor a_h and returns e^(hA)y+h(phi_1(hA)−phi_2(hA))g(t,y)+h phi_2(hA)g(t+h,a_h(t,y)).
For every d≥1 and X∈M_d(C), phi_1(X)=∫₀¹ exp((1−θ)X)dθ and phi_2(X)=∫₀¹ θ exp((1−θ)X)dθ, with componentwise integrals, including X=0.

For d≥1, a finite complex matrix A, 0≤s≤t≤T, an open realified time-state domain D, and a continuously differentiable solution y of y′=Ay+g(r,y(r)) with continuous forcing along the path, y(t)=exp((t−s)A)y(s)+∫ₛᵗ exp((t−r)A)g(r,y(r))dr.

For fixed T>0 and A, let K₊=sup₀≤r≤T ‖exp(rA)‖₂, K₋=sup₀≤r≤T ‖exp(−rA)‖₂ and κ=LK₊K₋. If g is L-Lipschitz on a common tube containing all compared states and stages, the transformed exponential-Euler and ETD2 maps have Lipschitz factors 1+κh and 1+h(κ+Tκ²/2), respectively, for 0<h≤T and admissible t.

A certified return from alg-certified-exponential-euler-etd2-step satisfies ‖computed step−exact method step‖₂≤δ_n. Its semigroup data give ‖phi_1(hA)‖₂≤B_h and ‖phi_2(hA)‖₂≤B_h/2. Under the declared finite-service and valid accounting contracts, the procedure terminates with 0≤C≤C_max and returns the sums of accrued actual service work counters.

For an exact solution with q(r)=g(r,y(r))∈C², bounds ‖q′‖₂≤Q₁ and ‖q″‖₂≤Q₂, and g L-Lipschitz on a tube containing the exact path and predictor, put C_E=K₊Q₁/2. For 0<h≤T, ‖Psi_h²(t,y(t))−y(t+h)‖₂≤K₊(Q₂+LC_E/2)h³.
If q(r)=g(r,y(r)) is continuously differentiable along the exact solution on [t,t+h], with ‖q′‖₂≤Q₁ and 0<h≤T, then ‖Psi_h^E(t,y(t))−y(t+h)‖₂≤K₊Q₁h²/2.
